approved: Ozone Protection and Synthetic Greenhouse Gas Management Reform (Closing the Hole in the Ozone Layer) Bill 2022
Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would rewrite the main law that controls who can import, export or make ozone-depleting substances and greenhouse gases.
It would move existing licence conditions into the legislation itself, clarify when a licence or exemption is needed, and give businesses more time to send reports and pay fees.

The compliance and enforcement powers would be brought into line with a standard Commonwealth framework, and the bill would add information-gathering notices, licence suspension and an internal review process.
Brings licence conditions such as the ban on non-refillable containers into the Act.
Clarifies licence and exemption rules to reduce accidental breaches.
Extends deadlines for submitting reports and paying levies.
Adopts the standard provisions of the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014.
Modernises the offence and penalty structure.
Introduces information-gathering powers including notices to produce.
Businesses that handle scheduled substances and individuals regulated under the Act.
